title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E526 studies transverse vibrations of an elastic rod (Euler–Bernoulli beam). The amplitude equation y'''' = y/f^4 has general solution y = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f), with ω = a/f. Case V, treated on the previous page, has one end pinned (u = 0: y = y'' = 0) and the other clamped (u = 1: y = y' = 0).

Pinned at u = 0. This kills cosh and cos, leaving y ∝ 2 sinh(uω) − K sin(uω).

Clamped at u = 1. The two conditions give the frequency equation tan ω = tanh ω. From it, sin²ω = tanh²ω/(1+tanh²ω) = sinh²ω/cosh 2ω. The coefficient needed for y(1) = 0 is therefore K = 2 sinh ω/|sin ω| = 2√(cosh 2ω) = √(2(e^{2ω}+e^{-2ω})). This is exactly Euler's Ω, and Euler is right to call it an exact 'formula irrationalis'.

Sign rule. The roots of tan ω = tanh ω have sin ω and cos ω of the same sign. Upper sign (−) applies when both are positive, lower (+) when both are negative. Euler approximates the roots as ω ≈ (4n+1)π/4.

§42 (Scholion). Euler writes the general motion as a superposition of all simple modes: y = Σ C^{(k)} sin(ζ^{(k)} + ω_k² c√(2gb) t/a²)·(2 sinh(uω_k) ∓ Ω_k sin(uω_k)). Each mode has its own arbitrary amplitude and phase, and its circular frequency is proportional to ω_k².

§43. Euler begins case VI, both ends clamped: y = 0 and y' = 0 at both ends. At u = 0 this gives δ = −α − β and γ = −α + β. The next page shows the frequency equation is cos ω cosh ω = 1, the same as the free–free case I, with roots approximated as ω ≈ (2n+1)π/2. The mode shape has the signs of γ and δ reversed relative to case I.
errors: In the general formula of §42 the hyperbolic part is printed as (e^{ω} − e^{−ω}), constant in u. It must be e^{uω} − e^{−uω}, i.e. 2 sinh(uω), as in the previous page's mode shape and as the boundary conditions require.
The factor c in the time-frequency appears only in the first term (ωωc√2gb/aa); the subsequent terms omit c. This is a typographical inconsistency.

Not an error on this page, but the root values ω = (4n+1)π/4 used for the sounds are approximations to the roots of tan ω = tanh ω. The fundamental root 3.9266 is very close to 5π/4 = 3.9270. Ω itself, however, is exact given the frequency equation.

ideas.what: Representation of the general free vibration of a beam as a superposition of normal modes with arbitrary amplitudes and phases
ideas.modern_name: modal superposition / eigenfunction expansion for the Euler–Bernoulli beam
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli (superposition principle, strings); Euler/D. Bernoulli for beams (1730s–1770s)
ideas.where_published: E526 itself; also Euler's earlier string papers and De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum (E443)

ideas.what: Exact closed form for the mode-shape coefficient of the pinned–clamped beam, Ω = √(2(e^{2ω}+e^{−2ω})) = 2√(cosh 2ω), with a sign rule according to the quadrant of ω
ideas.modern_name: normalized mode shape of the clamped–pinned (propped cantilever) beam, with frequency equation tan βL = tanh βL
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E443, E526); standard in Rayleigh's Theory of Sound

ideas.what: Clamped–clamped beam has the same frequency equation as the free–free beam (cos ω cosh ω = 1)
ideas.modern_name: clamped–clamped / free–free spectral coincidence for the Euler–Bernoulli beam
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (and D. Bernoulli); discussed in Truesdell's 1960 historical survey
ideas.where_published: E526 §43ff; also earlier treatments in E443

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard modal-superposition scholion and the opening of the clamped–clamped case. Both are well documented in E526 and in Truesdell's history of elasticity. The only noteworthy points are an exact closed form for the mode coefficient, which is elementary, and a misprint in the formula.
transcription_corrections: The image prints (e^{ω} − e^{−ω} ∓ Ω sin. u ω) in every term, and the transcription is faithful to that. Mathematically it should read e^{uω} − e^{−uω}; this is a misprint in the original.
'aequatio generalis erit' – correct; 'scribendo, vt hactenus, u loco s/a' – correct.
